Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation

Hi John (and Nora),

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the candid walkthrough of Acme Retail's inference pain points. Below is a short recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we all have the same expectations. Please reply with any corrections.

What we heard (pain & context)
- Recent incidents: two major incidents in last 6 months (one cache corruption incident causing degraded throughput ~8 hours; a separate regional throttling event during peak holiday traffic).
- Current stack: on-prem inference for low-latency storefront features, cloud fallback to a managed endpoint for burst traffic. KV cache lives on an in-house Redis cluster.
- Requirements: 95th p99 latency budget at <300ms for critical inference paths; need predictable availability during peak traffic; audit logs for all model calls and longer retention for debug traces.
- Constraints: procurement windows (quarterly), limited ops bandwidth for deep infra changes in next 90 days.

Success criteria (how you'll measure a pilot)
- End-to-end 95th latency maintained under 300ms for 90% of test traffic profile.
- No data loss during failover; successful automatic fallback to a secondary region + fallback model in <60s.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown + request tracing for top 10 slow traces within 24 hours.

Reliability & graceful degradation package we discussed
- Fallback model variants: quantized 7B model as warm standby for cold failures (degraded quality but high availability).
- Regional failover: primaries in us-west, warm standby in us-east with automated routing and health checks.
- Canary and rollout controls: canary at 1% traffic, automatic rollback on error-rate/latency thresholds.
- KV/prefix caching: optional managed prefix cache to reduce repeated cold starts and improve tail latency.
- SLAs: baseline 99.9% with an option to bump to 99.95% for an enterprise contract (details to confirm with legal).

Next steps (proposed)
1) I will share a mutual action plan (attached) with milestones for a 2-week technical pilot + 4-week validation phase.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra team to go over integration points (suggested: Wed 4/22 10am PT). Zoom link included in the next email.
3) We will provide: SOC2 summary, sample contracts (SLA tiers), and a ballpark price range for pilot and committed capacity.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MAP), reliability-matters-v1.pdf (brief on degradation strategies)

If this aligns, I’ll schedule the deep-dive and loop in Rishi and David for the technical session.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the thorough recap — this is very helpful and matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:
- Incident details: the cache corruption event also caused a cascade where a batch job re-wrote bad keys which increased latency across the cluster; it took ~8 hours to fully recover and clear the bad cache.
- Tolerance: for our checkout personalization path we need 95th percentile latency under 300ms; for search suggestions we can tolerate up to 500ms at 95th.
- Failover expectation: automatic failover is critical — manual intervention during peak is not acceptable.

What we'd like from Redwood next:
- A short architecture note on how the warm standby model will be kept in sync and how you handle cache invalidation during failover.
- A ballpark price for a 2-week pilot (estimate of peak RPS we provided on the call) and two SLA tiers.
- SOC2 docs and any relevant compliance materials.

Happy to move forward with the 4/22 deep-dive you suggested — Wed 4/22 10am PT works for our infra leads.

John / Nora,

Great — thanks for the clarifications. Quick answers below and a couple of operational notes before the deep-dive.

How the warm standby works (short):
- Model variants: we keep a quantized 7B model warm in the standby cluster (reduced memory footprint + fast cold-starts). Quality delta is small for non-critical prompts; we recommend an evaluation set to quantify impact for your checkout personalization.
- Cache strategy: managed prefix caching with write-through semantics during normal ops; during failover we switch to read-only mode on the primary cache and rely on the standby cache while replaying recent writes asynchronously. This avoids blocking traffic and provides eventual consistency for non-critical state.
- Invalidation: we support invalidation hooks via webhook or SDK calls so your batch jobs can trigger invalidation across both primary and standby caches.

SLA & pricing (ballpark)
- Pilot (2-week): estimated $6k–$10k depending on peak RPS and model selection (we’ll size GPUs once you confirm peak RPS).
- Production SLA tiers: 99.9% (standard) vs 99.95% (enterprise; includes 4x regional redundancy + SLO credits). Exact pricing depends on committed throughput.

Attachments: updated mutual-action-plan.xlsx (I added milestones and owners)

Tech deep-dive logistics
